clue.text: One in France turning indecent

parts.note: UN is the French masculine word for one
turning into something is becoming it, as in 'turning nasty'

explanation.surface: Someone in France is said to be going off the rails into lewd behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning' reads as part of the French scene but is simply a synonym for becoming.
explanation.definitionFit: Unbecoming behaviour is improper or unseemly, a mild sense of indecent.

clue.text: One texted: you idiot

parts.note: in text-message spelling 'you' is written as the single letter U
a nit is a British word for a fool

explanation.surface: A message reads like someone texting an insult to a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: NIT, short for nitwit, is everyday British slang for a silly person.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a single thing or the number one in counting, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Inventor and junior clamping a piece of lab equipment

parts.note: Alexander Graham Bell, inventor of the telephone

indicators.note: the abbreviation for junior grips the letter between its two letters, as a clamp holds something

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An inventor and his junior assistant hold a piece of laboratory apparatus in a clamp.
explanation.definitionFit: A bell jar is a glass dome used in laboratories to cover apparatus or hold a vacuum.

clue.text: Henry chats about mother's plant

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
MUM is the British word for mother; the 's is read as 'has'

explanation.surface: Henry gossips about the plant his mother keeps.
explanation.walkthrough: The plant is also nicknamed a mum, which makes the ending neat.
explanation.definitionFit: The chrysanthemum is a flowering garden plant of the daisy family.

clue.text: Flash meal is in vogue

parts.note: a flash is an instant, and MO is British slang for a moment
a dish is a course or meal served

explanation.surface: A showy dinner is described as fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flash' reads as the adjective meaning showy, but it is the noun for an instant: half a mo.
explanation.definitionFit: Modish means fashionable, the same as being in vogue.

clue.text: I see island after turning on rescue ship

indicators.note: the exclamation and island come after the turned word
turning the little word around makes it read backwards

parts.note: the word itself, taken as written
AH is an exclamation of understanding, like 'I see'
Sark is one of the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: Someone spots an island after switching something on, aboard a rescue vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: Sark is a small Channel Island between Guernsey and Jersey.
explanation.definitionFit: Noah's ark is the vessel in Genesis that saved Noah's family and the animals from the Flood.

clue.text: Give up fairly shortly

indicators.note: shortly says the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: quite means fairly, as in quite good

explanation.surface: Someone abandons something fairly soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shortly' looks like 'soon' but tells you to clip the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To quit is to abandon or stop, exactly what giving up means.

clue.text: Lift heart of adult with commendation

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter

parts.note: five letters, so its centre is a single letter
praise is commendation

explanation.surface: Encouraging an adult with praise lifts their spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: To upraise is an old verb for raising or elevating something, as a lift does.

clue.text: Electronic device starts iron when activated

indicators.note: activated suggests the letters are set in motion and rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An electrical gadget switches on an iron when someone turns it on.
explanation.definitionFit: A transistor is a semiconductor component used to amplify or switch signals in circuits.

clue.text: Crude bridle twisted around Lipizzaner's head

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the single letter
twisted means the letters of the harness word are bent into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a Lipizzaner is a white horse breed of the Spanish Riding School

explanation.surface: A rough bridle is twisted round a show horse's head.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-bred means badly brought up, coarse and rude in manners, so crude in that sense.

clue.text: Country area American ptarmigan regularly avoided

indicators.note: skipping every other letter of the bird's name, keeping the rest

parts.note: a grouse-like bird of cold mountains

explanation.surface: An American in some region steadily keeps away from the local game bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The kept letters are the second, fourth, sixth and eighth of the bird's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Austria is a nation in central Europe with Vienna as its capital.

clue.text: Calculation of understocked business branch?

parts.note: a shop that is understocked is short of goods
a division is a section of a company

explanation.surface: The question asks what to call the accounts of a poorly supplied part of a firm.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful reading of an arithmetic term.
explanation.definitionFit: Short division is a method of dividing numbers written out without the intermediate working.

clue.text: Classic text showing honest cry for help by Conservatives

parts.note: just means fair and honest
SOS is the distress signal
Tories are members of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A classic book appears to show an honest plea for aid from the Tories.
explanation.definitionFit: Kipling's Just So Stories (1902) is a famous children's book, a classic of literature.

clue.text: Fling cheat out — that's no contest for them

definitions.text: Fling cheat out — that's no contest for them

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters are reshuffled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Throw the cheat out of the ring: there is no contest for cheats.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: the anagram and the picture of a bout with any cheating banished.
explanation.definitionFit: A clean fight is a fair bout with no foul play, from which cheats are excluded.

clue.text: Large piece of jewellery on uniform is beguiling

indicators.note: in an across answer, the jewellery is placed after the letter it is said to be on

parts.note: a ring is worn on the finger

explanation.surface: A big ring worn with a uniform looks alluring.
explanation.walkthrough: U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Luring means enticing or tempting someone, the same as beguiling them.

clue.text: Stormy petrels eating unknown snacks

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take the letter inside them
stormy suggests the seabirds' letters are tossed about

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
Z is a mathematical unknown, like x and y

explanation.surface: Seabirds in a storm are feeding on unidentified nibbles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stormy petrels' reads as the bird name storm petrel, which hides the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretzels are knotted baked bread snacks, often salted.

clue.text: Dark brown beast eating figure up

indicators.note: the beast takes the number inside it

parts.note: a brute is a beast

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the number is written bottom to top

parts.note: ten is a figure, a number

explanation.surface: A dark brown animal is gobbling a number.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunette describes hair of a dark brown colour.

clue.text: Unconventional character's advanced attack about to be absorbed by emperor

parts.note: A is short for advanced, as in A level

indicators.note: the reversed attack is taken into the emperor's name

parts.note: Nero was a Roman emperor

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: to hit is to attack

explanation.surface: A brash character's forward assault is soaked up by an emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: An antihero is a central figure in fiction lacking the usual heroic virtues.

clue.text: Vessels and train contracted by delivery firm

indicators.note: contracted means shortened, losing its last letter

parts.note: to train someone is to teach them
UPS is the parcel delivery company

explanation.surface: Ships and a railway service are hired by a courier company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessels' and 'train' suggest transport, and 'contracted' a business deal, but the vessels are for drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Teacups are small drinking cups, and a vessel can be any container for liquid.

clue.text: This compiler's working in knockout garment

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the knockout abbreviation

parts.note: the setter speaks of himself as I, and 'I'm' is 'this compiler is'
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: The setter claims to be operating in a boxing knockout robe.
explanation.walkthrough: KO is the boxing abbreviation for a knockout.
explanation.definitionFit: A kimono is a long Japanese robe with wide sleeves, a traditional item of dress.

clue.text: Going to abandon outsiders, ruler sounding swinish

indicators.note: the word drops its outside letters, its first and last

parts.note: the word whose inner letters are kept
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: A ruler, about to desert those outside the court, is behaving like a pig.
explanation.definitionFit: Oinking is the grunting noise a pig makes, so making a swinish noise.

clue.text: Swimmer's battle to cross lake before you and me

indicators.note: the battle-and-lake piece comes before the pronoun
the battle word stretches across the letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a war is a battle on a grand scale
us means you and me

explanation.surface: A swimmer struggles to get across a lake ahead of the two of us.
explanation.definitionFit: A walrus is a large tusked marine mammal that swims in Arctic waters.

clue.text: Disintegrating stuff, ragmen tat I once sampled

indicators.note: sampled means only part of the phrase is taken, the run of letters across its words

parts.note: the phrase containing the answer

explanation.surface: Someone once tried out the falling-apart junk of rag-and-bone men.
explanation.walkthrough: A ragman collected and sold old rags; tat is cheap rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Fragmentation is the process of breaking into pieces, the gerund sense of disintegrating.

clue.text: Food items King George's taken from bakery

indicators.note: the royal initials are removed from the bakery's name

parts.note: Greggs is a British high-street chain of bakeries
GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George; the 's is 'has'

explanation.surface: A royal George has some food items taken from a baker's shop.
explanation.walkthrough: Greggs is a well-known British bakery chain selling sausage rolls and pasties.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs are basic foodstuffs laid by hens, each one a food item.

clue.text: Foodie's gut more volatile

indicators.note: volatile means unstable, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A food lover's stomach is getting more temperamental.
explanation.definitionFit: A gourmet is a connoisseur of fine eating, now often called a foodie.

clue.text: Irritating being blocked by a barrier

indicators.note: the single letter stands in the way, sitting inside the word

parts.note: riling means annoying or irritating
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something annoying is being stopped by a fence.
explanation.definitionFit: A railing is a fence of bars, a barrier.

clue.text: Mission created by armoured vehicle changing direction

indicators.note: one compass point, north, is swapped for another, south

parts.note: a tank is an armoured military vehicle

explanation.surface: A military assignment is carried out by a tank that turns round.
explanation.walkthrough: N and S are compass directions, so 'changing direction' swaps one for the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A task is a job or assignment, which is what a mission is.

clue.text: A younger relative gets older people

parts.note: per means 'a', as in ten pounds per head
a son is a relative of a younger generation
to age is to get older

explanation.surface: A junior family member grows up to join the older generation.
explanation.walkthrough: PER replaces 'a' as in 'twice a day' = 'twice per day'.
explanation.definitionFit: Personages are persons, especially important ones, so a formal word for people.
